title: Designing a Chat System: Delivery, Ordering, and Presence
lesson:
A chat system maintains persistent connections (typically WebSockets) between clients and a fleet of gateway servers. Because a recipient may be connected to any gateway, the system needs a way to route a message to the right one: commonly a session registry (user to gateway mapping, often in a fast store like Redis) plus a pub/sub or message bus that forwards the message to that gateway. If the recipient is offline, the message is persisted and delivered, with a push notification, when they reconnect.

Delivery guarantees are usually at-least-once: the sender retries until the server acknowledges, and the receiver acknowledges on receipt. Retries create duplicates, so each message carries a client-generated unique ID and the server deduplicates on it. Delivery and read receipts are just more small messages flowing back along the same path.

Ordering matters inside a conversation, not globally. A common approach is to assign each message a monotonically increasing sequence number per conversation, generated by whichever node owns that conversation (for example by partitioning on conversation ID). Clients sort by that sequence and detect gaps to fetch missing messages. Using client wall-clock timestamps for ordering is fragile because of clock skew.

Storage is write-heavy and read-by-recent-range, which fits wide-column or log-structured stores keyed by conversation ID and sequence. Presence (online/offline, typing) is ephemeral, so it is kept in memory with heartbeats and TTLs rather than durable storage, and fan-out is limited, for example by only pushing presence to a user's active contacts, because large groups would otherwise generate enormous update traffic.

questions.prompt: A message's recipient is connected to a different gateway server than the sender. What is a typical way to deliver it?
options: Have the sender open a direct connection to the recipient
Look up the recipient's gateway in a session registry and forward via a message bus
Broadcast the message to every user
Wait for the recipient to poll the database
questions.explanation: A user-to-gateway registry plus pub/sub lets any server route a message to the gateway holding the recipient's connection.

questions.prompt: Because retries can deliver the same message twice, each message carries a client-generated unique ID so the server can ____ it.
questions.explanation: At-least-once delivery causes duplicates, which idempotent handling by message ID removes.

questions.prompt: Ordering messages by each client's local timestamp is a reliable way to order a conversation.
questions.explanation: Client clocks drift and can be wrong, so a per-conversation sequence number assigned server-side is more reliable.

questions.prompt: Why is presence data (online/typing) usually kept in memory with TTLs rather than durable storage?
options: It is ephemeral and changes constantly, so durability adds cost without value
It needs strong consistency across regions
questions.explanation: Presence is short-lived state refreshed by heartbeats, so expiring in-memory entries are cheaper and sufficient.

questions.prompt: Order the path of a message to an offline recipient, earliest first.
items: Recipient reconnects and fetches pending messages
Server persists the message and acknowledges the sender
Sender submits the message to a gateway
A push notification is sent to the recipient's device
questions.explanation: The message is accepted and stored first, the device is nudged, and delivery completes when the recipient reconnects.
